subject: BlueHarbor follow-up: DPA variant, SCC module preference & VSQ kickoff
messages:
From: Alice Grant <alice.grant@blueharbor.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: 2027-06-28T15:12:00-04:00
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's demo — GDPR/DPA questions

Hi Vanessa / Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the latency and routing examples were helpful. Procurement and legal asked for a few items so we can move the deal to contracting:

- Can you confirm Redwood's SOC 2 status (type II or type I, date of last audit)?
- For GDPR: do you have a preferred DPA variant and which SCC module do you expect we should sign (Controller-to-Processor vs Processor-to-Processor)?
- We also want to kick off the vendor security questionnaire (VSQ) — can you provide the intake link or a contact to complete it?

I've attached our standard risk intake form so you have context on what procurement will look at. Goal from our side: get the DPA + SCC decision and an initial VSQ response within two weeks so procurement can package the PO.

Appreciate a short confirmation and any templates you can share.

Thanks,
Alice Grant
Head of Security Operations
BlueHarbor Financial

Attachment: blueharbor_risk_form.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alice Grant <alice.grant@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: 2027-06-28T16:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo — GDPR/DPA questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below.

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II audit in April 2027. I've attached a one-page summary of scope and the auditor statement (redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf). We can share the full report under NDA if needed.

2) DPA & SCC module: our standard approach is to execute a Controller-to-Processor DPA when the customer is the data controller (typical for SaaS customers). We provide an EU SCC implementation using the Controller-to-Processor module. If BlueHarbor prefers alternate routing (e.g., processor-to-processor chain), we can map to that — but most customers sign the Controller-to-Processor module with Redwood as Processor.

3) VSQ: we've got a short intake we use to triage (link below). If you prefer, we can start by filling the questionnaire on your behalf and then book a 30-min triage call with our security lead.

Suggested next steps:
- I attach our current DPA template (redwood_DPA_template_v3.docx) for your legal to review.
- If you confirm BlueHarbor will be Controller, we'll prepare the Controller-to-Processor SCC module addendum and return a redline within 3 business days.
- We can begin VSQ intake immediately — please confirm the preferred contact.

Related links:
Vendor security questionnaire intake: https://drive.redwood.com/VSQ/BlueHarbor
DPA template (read-only): https://app.redwood.com/legal/dpa/templates/v3

I'll loop in Lauren from Legal Ops (cc) to help with turnaround on the DPA.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf, redwood_DPA_template_v3.docx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alice Grant <alice.grant@blueharbor.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: 2027-06-29T09:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo — GDPR/DPA questions

Thanks everyone — a couple of technical clarifications from the infra side that may affect the DPA appendix:

- Data flows: Redwood typically processes request payloads and short-lived KV cache entries. We can enable a no-logs profile for BlueHarbor if you want to avoid retention of conversational logs.
- Retention & exports: we support configurable retention windows; if you need limited retention for compliance we can set a 30-day default and provide export/secure-delete tooling. See attached options.
- HIPAA: if you need HIPAA-level controls (BAA), that generally requires either a Private deployment or an enterprise agreement with specific config controls — happy to scope separately if relevant.

For SCC module choice: Controller-to-Processor is the cleanest route for most customers where BlueHarbor controls the data class and processing instructions. If anything in your legal review suggests BlueHarbor is acting as a joint controller for processed outputs, we should flag that now and plan for additional mapping.

I've attached a short note on retention profiles and examples we provide for legal (data_retention_options.pdf). Happy to join a call with your security/legal to walk through specifics.

-Jordan
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachment: data_retention_options.pdf
From: Alice Grant <alice.grant@blueharbor.com>

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo — GDPR/DPA questions

Thanks — that timeline works. Procurement and legal want us to proceed as follows:

- Please produce the DPA with the Controller-to-Processor SCC module (BlueHarbor will be Controller).
- Start the VSQ intake using this contact: legal@blueharbor.com. If you fill the VSQ for us, we will validate the answers on our triage call.
- Confirm SOC 2 Type II as April 2027 (we'll route for internal audit). If you can provide the SOC 2 summary to procurement that helps.

Target: we need a signed DPA in procurement by 2027-07-14 to meet the July P.O. cycle. Can you commit to delivering a DPA redline by 2027-07-01 and a VSQ draft within 3 business days of intake?

If yes, we'll schedule a 30-min legal/security triage early next week.

Best,
Alice Grant
Head of Security Operations
BlueHarbor Financial
